newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO under pressure as crude slumps.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO under pressure as crude slumps.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Tuesday were expected to remain under pressure as crude prices continued its three-day downward trend, traders said.
They said there were no shortage of supplies in Asia as South Korean refiners continued to produce substantial volumes for exports.

Purchases by China for December arrival of 180-cst cargoes have largely been supplied by the Koreans with deals done around $7.00 per tonne over Singapore spot quotes or $124 per tonne, on a cost-and-freight basis to Southern China.

Traders said talking levels in singapore on Tuesday would slip as much as $1.00 below the deal done on Monday at $118 a tonne between a U.S. major and a Singapore trader for a December 9-13 cargo of 180-cst fuel oil, on a free-on-board basis.
They expect the same U.S. major that has been selling since Friday to show up with offers again later Tuesday.
SIMEX fuel oil futures traded at $118.50 per tonne for December, down 50 cents from its previous close, with five lots recorded at 0752 GMT.
Swaps levels edged lower with December traded at $117.50 and quoted at $116.50/$117.50, down from Monday's $117.00/$118.00.
